answers.text: Any of the narcotic analgesics (opioids) like codeine, morphine, tramadol, or oxycodone would be a very effective cough suppressant, but unless strong pain is also an issue, they would not be the preferred therapy for relieving cough.

params.textField: If a person has a non-productive cough, they can be given one of the antitussives (cough suppressants) that work at the level of the medulla. In that case, a *cough suppressant* like *dextromethorphan* should be used. However, if their cough is associated with sputum, it should never be suppressed. Instead, the client should be given one of the agents that helps excrete the mucus from the lungs. *expectorants* like *guaifenesin (like Benadryl) * prompt the lungs to release more thin secretions. Alternatively, *mucolytic agents* like *acetylcysteine* break up the molecular bonds in the mucus. Either of those medications will help get thick mucus out of the lungs.
